This is a double-edged sword as the Pursuit was way more consistent than the Ace Pilot, but fast enemies often just walked right past it. It also had the same placement limit, being 10. Anyways, as for the stats, it was quite cheap for the DPS it dealt, though the DPS was hampered quite a lot by the ROF bug though. matches.title: In defense of Mystery...
matches.snippet: In defense of Mystery... Over the years, Mystery has been receiving unnecessary hate and the Breaker has been admired for replacing it. I've been in lobbies[trio & quad], and solo matches and just go without a plan and have never leaked nor struggled to breaker[the only splash I've seen are Jester, Pursuit missiles, and max ranger]. So much for making people "strategize" and use "splash damage," huh? Not only that, but you know it's going to spawn more breakers while being aware you have the DPS to kill them off. How about mystery? In modern TDS landscape[which is where I'm basing it off for both mystery & breaker], RNG isn't an issue. matches.snippet: Which loadout are you taking...? The tactician loadout is good in terms of versatility, being able to handle early, mid, and late game relatively well. however, it underperforms as it takes most all-rounder towers over troops that excel within the niche, meaning that this loadout is surprisingly good for solos compared to trios or quads. matches.title: Expanding TDS' Economy
matches.snippet: Expanding TDS' Economy Introduction TDS only has three economy towers, and one of them is just a downgraded version of another - it won't even be considered here. The Golden Cowboy and Farm have had a varied place in the meta over time, whether it be amidst countless rebalances or none at all. These towers allow you to spend money to get more money in return - it's hard for them to be 'bad' towers due to this simple positive loop. Despite this simplicity, there are only two economy towers in the game - I'm surprised we don't have more, with unique mechanics stacked onto them - currently we only have a tower that generates cash and a tower that shoots and generates cash. Yes, adding new economy towers would likely be a balancing nightmare, as shown by the current two we already have, but it would help make the game more interesting, I'd reckon. This hypothetical suggests that economy towers be the norm and get more focus, and more towers filling the role. Naturally, a few other things need to be changed before this can be done. The Baseline As of currently, the Farm and Golden Cowboy are modest towers, quite strong but not that overpowered - you don't need the extra cash sometimes. matches.title: [REWORK] Golden Towers (+ Base towers)
matches.snippet: [REWORK] Golden Towers (+ Base towers) Ever since golden towers came into existence, they have been unbalanced. They're usually better than the base tower or other towers (like soldier and militant) or a direct upgrade from the base tower (pyro). Because of this, 9/10 you will be using the golden version of the tower and never the base form tower after getting the golden skin of it. These reasons are definitely why there hasn't been a new golden tower since 2020. I believe to solve this isn't to make the base tower stronger but rather make golden skins a more of a remix version of the tower, granting new abilities, gimmicks and stats themed around the based tower. I'll see if I can update this post later with links to new stats for a more detailed page. Here is some examples: Scout Base scout is the current golden scout, however the amount of money gained from selling it is 90% cash back instead of 1/3. This let's scout be a early game tower that can be easily replaced with other towers. Golden scout is a weaker version of the base scout except the value of selling it goes up in each wave (E.g., wave 0 it's 30 cash, wave 1 it's 33). However the tower needs to be placed for the value to go up, meaning a g-scout place on wave 0 is 33 cash in wave 1, placing another g-scout will start at 30 cash.

But honestly, the tower is just… unreliable. The skeletons spawned by the ability are completely random every time, and the ability also kills the previously spawned skeletons and periodically stops the Necromancer from attacking, and even then the skeletons die easily when not used right. Don’t get me wrong, the tower is fun to use, especially and can be strong when used right at max level, but it’s just not really reliable. It lands a spot on high C tier.
